steps.title: Fleet workshop and boat presentation
steps.outcome: Compare and prepare a purposeful fit on an existing owned hull, review its real bill and install it using paid work and physical equipment.
features: Fleet fitting workspace with numbered sockets, physical arcs and before/after capacity, deployment, stores and daily obligations.
Knowledge-only named templates and atomic paid fitting using real lockers, harbor materials, workers, experts and purses.
Original hull and equipment detail across the existing 24 hulls, sharing stable socket origins with aim and effects.

steps.title: Tactical roles, encirclement and harassment
steps.outcome: Light craft coordinate useful firing passes and breakaways while screens, heavies and explicit commands provide credible counters.
features: Role-aware target and reachable station decisions using actual weapons, observed threats, objectives and escape costs.
Coordinated pressure, fixed-tube strike alignment, regrouping and doctrine with authoritative manual orders.
Bounded decisions and recorded A1-A5 motion, counterexamples and both team orientations.

steps.title: Damageable weapons and machinery
steps.outcome: Physical weapon, propulsion and pump failures change combat and survival, and persist through repair, refit and saves.
features: Localized condition and disable state for actual fitted mount IDs, propulsion and pumps.
Crew repair priorities consume finite time, supplies and paid work without resetting condition through swaps.
Doctrine reacts to actual system loss, fire and flooding, with readable causes and repair choices.

steps.title: Convoy breakthroughs and recovery battles
steps.outcome: Physical carriers escape with their actual manifests and damaged hulls can be extracted, abandoned or lost with once-only custody.
features: Navigable convoy exits and per-carrier objective results with bounded armed and unarmed deployment.
Recovery encounters reuse real boarding, prize, tow, wreck and crew ownership.
Aftermath choices reconcile actual losses, manifests, repair costs and escrow exactly once.

steps.title: Autonomous fleet conflict, sightings and pursuit
steps.outcome: Observed pirate, patrol and faction encounters run without the player nearby and retain one canonical lifecycle and ledger.
features: Dated personal/shared observations guide physical search, pursuit, interception, joining and retreat.
Participant hostility graphs, exclusive hull reservations and persistent encounter transitions prevent duplicate battles or prizes.
Calibrated distant resolution and paid recovery preserve real condition, stores, crews and budgets.

steps.title: Coastal geography and large-hull navigation
steps.outcome: Original regional terrain supports feasible light/heavy approaches, exits and large civilian hull envelopes.
features: Roadstead, island passage and reef approach use repeatable encounter-region geometry and readable landmarks.
Hull eligibility and geometry revision participate in route feasibility and cache keys.
Copy-first voyage migration preserves identities, paid routes and inventories without land spawns or disconnected fallbacks.

steps.title: Civilian hull progression
steps.outcome: Twelve original civilian designs have physical layouts, honest paid construction and useful hull-specific capacities.
features: Three fishing, four cargo, two tanker and three yacht designs extend the 24 preserved original hull IDs.
Distinct working decks, scale, crew, stores, machinery, hold, tankage and guest accommodation have real costs.
Fitting, laboratory, navigation, custody and old-save schemas cover the actual delivered roster without minting assets.

steps.title: Working civilian voyages, piracy and rivals
steps.outcome: Fishing, freight, tanker transfers and funded yacht charters use vulnerable real manifests and finite owners.
features: Affordable ordinary-asset fishing and haulage loops use actual work, source depletion, demand and buyer purses.
Timed partial fuel transfers and passenger/baggage custody survive interruption, capture, loss and saves.
Independent civilian, pirate and escort decisions coexist with bounded witnessed captain memories and paid recovery.

steps.title: Supplied faction operations
steps.outcome: Funded faction objectives move real supplies, crews and hulls through vulnerable routes and sustainable operations.
features: Bounded coordinated patrol, raid, escort and supply objectives consume actual owner budgets and logistics.
Physical arrivals, interdiction and losses affect readiness and construction instead of granting free reinforcements.
Independent relations, civilian custody and player career choices remain consistent through operations and saves.

steps.title: AI quality, progression, polish and performance
steps.outcome: The complete behavior matrix, six representative careers and declared CPU/load targets have separate reproducible evidence.
features: Validate explorer, merchant, escort, privateer, fisher and passenger careers plus tanker and large-hull support cases.
Held-out adverse fixtures cover A1-A9, economic shocks, serial/worker publication and calibrated near/distant outcomes.
Review original presentation and motion separately from source checks, CPU measurements, audio, export and publication.
